evidence.title: What Stage 3 found
evidence.licence: MIT for the code. The content is the project's own analysis; it quotes public data under each source's licence, as the atlas's data page lists them.
evidence.text:
- **Filing without an attorney still goes with far fewer grants.** With the route, year, state and co-filers held together, Australian individuals' patents filed alone are granted 31.2 points less often (35.8 raw), in both decades; trade marks and designs with no agent before the first renewal are less often in force after it. Not a cause: an application dropped early may never appoint an attorney. Observations: M1, M2.
- **Australian organisations' patents: three readings that still disagree.** At the same reach they are less likely to end (hazard ratios 0.648 to 0.811), yet they reach fewer offices and are cited about 27% to 30% less at the same reach, field, route and year. None of the three is value; they must be read together. Observations: M3, M4.

section: Step 4 of 4: From the data to the observation (4 reasoning steps)
evidence.text:
The steps are not findings; only the last is.

1. Take Stage 2's comparison (filed alone against with an attorney) as the raw figure.
2. Fit one model of the yes or no outcome (granted or not) with the route, filing year, state and co-filers held together, and report the difference as an average difference in points.
3. Compare the held figure with the raw one, and give the outcome by Stage 3's rule (holds if at least half remains and the interval is clear of zero).
4. Repeat in the earlier decade, among applications with a field (holding the field), and among examined applications.

**Which gives observation M1:** Australian individuals' standard patents filed alone are granted 31.2 points less often than those filed with an attorney once the route, filing year, state and co-filers are held together (FY2010 to FY2019), against 35.8 points with nothing held: 87.2% of Stage 2's gap remains, and 86.2% in the earlier decade. Trade marks filed alone show the same gap for individuals and organisations alike, almost untouched by what is held.

evidence.title: Overview: what Australia's IP data show so far
evidence.licence: MIT for the code. The content is the project's own analysis; it quotes public data under each source's licence, as the atlas's data page lists them.
evidence.text:
- **Australians, above all individuals, often file without an attorney.** Overseas filers use an attorney for 99.0% of standard patents, Australian filers for 85.4%, and Australian individuals file 62.4% of their trade marks alone. Observations: U20, U48.
- **Provisional applications doubled in FY2026.** 10,069 against 4,143 to 5,047 a year before, mostly from individuals but from organisations too, both broadly and through a few heavy filers. It is in the filings, not the recording. Why is a question for IP Australia. Observations: U8.
- **Around some policy changes, filing shows clear rushes, steps and pauses.** Rushes to file before a rule changed (Raising the Bar, 4.41 times Australians' usual month; the innovation patent's closure, 4.31 times), steps, and pauses when new Acts began; around other changes nothing stands out. These timings are the raw material for the natural experiments the later questions need. Observations: U28, U3.

evidence.title: U2: Five problems in the register were repaired before anything was measured
evidence.licence: MIT for the code. The content is the project's own analysis; it quotes public data under each source's licence, as the atlas's data page lists them.
section: Step 4 of 4: From the data to the observation (5 reasoning steps)
evidence.text:
The steps are not findings; only the last is.

1. Look for dates that cannot be true (before the register began, or a computer's default date).
2. Compare trade marks' registration dates with their filing dates before 1986.
3. Compare the "technology area" with the class for every type of right.
4. For each right, check whether its agent is one of its own applicants, by identity number or by name.
5. Recount attorney use without those self-agents.

**Which gives observation U2:** Profiling found five quirks: a false end date (1 January 1970) on 1,282 rights; one trade mark registered before the register began; 121,207 old trade marks "registered" on the day they were filed; a "technology area" that only repeated the class for trade marks and designs; and an attorney flag that counted applicants as their own attorneys. Each was repaired.

evidence.text:
8. The business or person who **filed** a right is kept beside the one who **holds** it now.
   - _Why:_ "Who files, and from where" and "who holds it now" are different questions; rights are often sold.
9. Each right's milestones come only from events the register still holds as standing (not later reversed), with placeholder and impossible dates left out.

pool.text:
- **Filing without an attorney goes with poorer outcomes.** Australian individuals' standard patents filed alone are granted about 36 percentage points less often, in both decades and among examined applications too. Australians' trade marks with no agent before the first renewal stay in force less often (19.1 points). The arrow may run backwards: an application abandoned early may never appoint an attorney. - **Some inventions made here are filed or held overseas.** About one patent in seven with an inventor in Australia is filed from overseas. Australian-filed patents now held only overseas are more common among the wide and the granted, though by firm the youngest filers are not clearly different. pool.text:
Stage 3's first table, for the research owner's review (section 8 of the Stage 3 notebook). Each signal is an association that survived its third factors held together, in both samples unless marked; none is a cause, and adopting any as a conclusion is the owner's decision.

- **Filing alone goes with far fewer grants (Australian individuals' standard patents, about 31 points), and no agent before the first renewal with fewer trade marks and designs in force after it, with the factors settled at filing held.** Observations: B5, B6, B10, M1, M2. Beyond the mechanics, the screen points to pairs that bear on the questions: patents filed without an attorney are more often withdrawn; how many countries a patent family reaches varies with the route, the applicant's country and the technology; women's share among inventors varies with the technology; and attorney markets are local.

- **Origin and reach:** the offices a standard patent's family is filed in vary with its route (0.431; 0.481), the applicant's country (0.386; 0.489) and the technology (0.328; 0.31: organic fine chemistry a median of 11). Followed up in B11 and B12.
- **Technology and inventors' gender:** women's estimated share varies with the technology (0.268; 0.297), highest in biotechnology. The apparent links with China are a quirk of the name dictionary (U97), not a finding. Followed up in B17 and B18.

With no agent recorded before the first renewal, 31.7% of Australians' trade marks filed FY2010 to FY2015 were in force after 10 years, against 50.8% with an attorney. With the filer's type, class, state, route and cohort held together the gap is 14.4 points, 75.5% of the raw 19.1; within individuals and within organisations it holds more fully. Designs show the same at their five-year renewal, almost untouched by what is held.

- **Within each type of filer** the gap holds more fully (85.3% to 94.6% left): individuals -11.8 and -12.0 points, organisations -15.1 and -10.8. Part of the pooled gap is who files alone: individuals, whose marks are less often in force either way (22.3% and 35.6% in FY2010 to FY2015).
- **Designs after 5 years**, FY2010 to FY2019: 30.0% against 46.7%, -16.7 raw and -16.3 held together in the first half; 32.4% against 46.8%, -14.5 and -14.1 in the second.
- B10's raw figures are reproduced (31.7% against 50.8%).

pool.title: U44: A few firms file most of the patents that firms file
pool.licence: MIT for the code. The content is the project's own analysis; it quotes public data under each source's licence, as the atlas's data page lists them.
pool.text:
- **Assumption:** One ABN is one firm. Companies in the same corporate group are counted separately, so concentration by corporate group would be at least as high as shown.
- **Assumption:** Applications without a filer's ABN (individuals, and some organisations) are outside this count; the shares describe firms with an ABN.
- **Limit:** A count of applications says nothing about their value. Heavy filers' patents may be worth more or less than anyone else's.
- **Limit:** Firms' IP counts are lower bounds (U41), and filers after FY2024 are less often linked to an ABN (U45).

pool.title: M2: Trade marks and designs with no agent before the first renewal are less often in force after it, once other factors are held
pool.licence: MIT for the code. The content is the project's own analysis; it quotes public data under each source's licence, as the atlas's data page lists them.
section: Step 3 of 4: How it was prepared (2 steps for this observation, on the IP rights lens)
pool.text:
2. Standard patents, provisional applications and second-tier (innovation and petty) patents are counted apart everywhere, and headline figures use standard patents.
   - _Why:_ They are different rights. A provisional is a cheap placeholder that is never granted; a second-tier patent is a cheaper, shorter right. Adding them together hides what each is doing.
3. Two placeholder dates are emptied (an end date of 1 January 1970 on 1,282 rights, and one registration before the register began).
   - _Why:_ 1 January 1970 is the "zero" of computer dates, standing in for an unknown date, not a real one.
4. Trade marks registered before 1986 have no "days to registration".
   - _Why:_ The register holds only their filing date, so their recorded time to registration is almost always zero.
5. The "technology area" is kept for patents only.
   - _Why:_ For every trade mark and design it simply repeated the class of goods, so it measured nothing new.
6. An attorney counts only if the agent on record is not the applicant itself.
   - _Why:_ The register's "agent" is the address for service, which is often the applicant's own; counting it said every trade mark had an attorney.

pool.title: M6: Granted Australian-founded patents are more often now held only overseas, at the same reach and filer type
pool.licence: MIT for the code. The content is the project's own analysis; it quotes public data under each source's licence, as the atlas's data page lists them.
pool.text:
Of standard patents first filed by an Australian applicant, the granted are more often now held only overseas than those never granted, with reach, the filer's type, field, route, year and co-filers held together: +5.6 points (FY2003 to FY2011) and +2.8 (FY2012 to FY2021). The wide patents' higher rate is more than halved once grant and type are held, and organisations' gap goes in the later period.

- **Granted against never granted:** +8.8 raw and +5.6 held together; +3.9 and +2.8. Holds in both, 63.9% and 70.4% left.
- **Five or more offices against Australia only:** +10.8 and +4.3; +5.1 and +2.2. Weakened: much of the wide patents' higher rate goes with their being granted and organisations'.
- **Organisations against individuals:** +5.3 and +2.6, weakened; +1.0 and +0.05, not detected once held in the later period.
- **Two endpoints, not transfers:** grant and reach are seen today, not necessarily before the holder changed, and nothing here says where value goes. The later period has had less time for holders to change.
